payload.claim: Spin-offs of S&P 500 companies that the index does not keep are sold by index funds at their first close, and earn a positive abnormal return from the next session's close through two sessions after.
payload.mechanism: The traders who buy the shares the index funds are forced to dump at the spin-off's first close are middlemen who can't afford to hold a small, risky new stock, so they sell it to me below fair value for about 2 days until they've unloaded.
payload.name: spinoff-orphan-forced-selling
payload.notes: Sealed 2026-10-14. Two regimes pooled (pre-2015 dispersed selling, post-2015 a single closing sale) because the 26 post-2015 events alone resolve only ~4.9% at the 11-day sigma and could not reach the 2.5% bar. Window shortened from 2-10 to 2-3 on his mechanism (unloading lasts ~2 days); the 2.5% bar was deliberately NOT moved with it. Run once with run_event_study.py --final; RUN.lock enforces it.
payload.universe: CRSP CIZ daily US common stock (crucible's CIZ common-stock filter), 1990-2025. Events: distributions with DisType SP and DisDetailType SECSO whose parent is an S&P 500 member on the ex-date; the spinco is a new listing whose first daily observation (its first regular-way trade, offset 0) is within 5 days of the ex-date, is US common stock that day, and is NOT an S&P 500 member on the next session. 105 events: 79 before 2015-10-01, 26 after (14 one-day members under S&P DJI's post-2015 spin-off rule, 12 never added). Abnormal = return minus the equal-weighted investable mean. Traded window: offsets 2-3, i.e. buy at the day-1 close, sell at the day-3 close.

payload.label: event study; the sharpe field holds the t-statistic across events
